paper.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks

objective: Reproduce, using this repository, the Cora test accuracy of the GCN in the 'GCN (rand. splits)' row of Table 2.

expected.why: The code runs fine but is a re-implementation with its own fixed split (140 train / 300 val / 1000 test taken from cora.content order) and no random-split evaluation; its test accuracy (about 0.82-0.84) is above the paper's number and outside tolerance. The README itself says it is not intended for reproduction of the paper's results.
expected.note: runs vary by about 0.01-0.02 between repeats even with the same --seed (sparse ops), hence 5 seeds are recorded

notes: Table 2 of arXiv 1609.02907 (pdftotext): 'GCN (this paper)  70.3 (7s)  81.5 (4s)  79.0 (38s)  66.0 (48s)' and 'GCN (rand. splits)  67.9 ± 0.5  80.1 ± 0.5  78.9 ± 0.7  58.4 ± 1.7' (columns Citeseer, Cora, Pubmed, NELL). The claim here is the Cora entry of the 'GCN (rand. splits)' row. Run from the pygcn/ package directory with the repo root on PYTHONPATH (`cd pygcn && PYTHONPATH=/mnt python3 train.py --no-cuda --seed S`): data path is `../data/cora/` and the package is imported as `pygcn.*` (README: `python setup.py install`). No code patch needed. The headline 81.5 entry ('GCN (this paper)') is NOT used as a claim because the repo's mean (~0.825) sits about at the tolerance edge for it and would make the ground truth noisy.
